Andy Ellis

Green candidate for Governor / Lt. Governor, Maryland · Challenger

Debate coach and owner of Debate Strategies LLC; former tech-sector worker

Andy Ellis is a Northeast Baltimore resident and co-chair of the Maryland Green Party. He filed for governor in Annapolis in September 2025 with running mate Owen Silverman Andrews. He won the Green Party's nomination in an online party primary held July 8–22, 2026.

Where Ellis stands

Data centers
Says data centers have no place in Maryland. Supports tighter regulation of the sector, ending subsidies, and halting all future data center construction.
Energy / climate
Proposes declaring climate, environment, energy, food and water emergencies so that state and local governments act with urgency.
Economy and jobs
Proposes developing a "solidarity economy" and investing in people and communities.
Elections / voting
Supports public campaign financing. Testified in favor of HB 101 on televised gubernatorial debates, arguing that Maryland Public Television's 10% polling threshold shuts out third-party candidates.
Reparations
Includes slavery reparations in his campaign platform.
Civic engagement
Proposes building a culture of civic engagement in which residents shape decisions through public debate, dialogue and collective action.

Background

  • Green Party nominee for Governor of Maryland, 2026 (nominated July 2026)
  • Co-chair, Maryland Green Party and Baltimore City Green Party; Green Party leadership roles since 2015
  • Green Party candidate for Maryland House of Delegates, District 45, 2018
  • Member, Baltimore City Charter Review Commission, 2023–2024
  • Chair, Baltimore For Democracy (committee opposing Question H), 2024
  • Debate coach; led Towson University to a national debate championship in 2008
  • Nearly 15 years in the corporate tech sector; founded Debate Strategies LLC
  • Education: Thomas Johnson High School (Frederick); attended Towson University and St. Mary's College of Maryland
